message.content:
Sure! Here’s a quick way to add that comment to the IP `192.168.1.1` on VirusTotal using a simple `curl` command (or a short Python snippet if you prefer).  
Just replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with your actual key (`ABC321` in this case) and run it from a terminal.

---

## 1. Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "type": "comment",
           "attributes": {
             "text": "Confirmed #malware"
           }
         }'
```

**What it does**

- Sends a `POST` request to the VirusTotal API endpoint for comments on the specified IP.
- Includes your API key in the `x-apikey` header.
- Sends the JSON payload you provided.

If everything goes well, you’ll receive a JSON response that looks something like:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "some-comment-id",
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
      "text": "Confirmed #malware",
      "created_at": "2026-07-09T12:34:56Z",
      ...
    }
  }
}
```

---

## 2. Using Python (requests)

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": "ABC321",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

response = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())
```

---

### Quick checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Replace `ABC321` with your real API key (you already have it). |
| ✅ | Make sure you’re connected to the internet. |
| ✅ | The IP address `192.168.1.1` is correctly formatted. |
| ✅ | The comment text matches what you want to submit. |

That’s all you need! Once you run the command or script, the comment will be attached to the IP record on VirusTotal. If you hit any errors, let me know the error message and I can help troubleshoot.
